descriptions.preferred: The outstanding features of this cultivar are its color and vigor. The leaf color is the rich red orange of the gemstone garnet. When this maple is grown in shade, the leaves retain a greenish cast, but in a sunny location the garnet color develops well. It is a vigorous-growing form eventually attaining a height of 4 m or more. When very heavily fertilized, the plant sends out new shoots up to 1 m on young plants. In the landscape, however, the shoots are not as long, and the plant shapes itself well. It has the pendulous, spreading habit of dissectums, and as it matures forms a beautiful, cascading, mound-shaped specimen. The leaves are large for a dissectum, and the deep color holds well into the summer season. Well-fertilized young plants have leaf lobes up to 12 cm long, although most are shorter. Each of the seven lobes separates entirely to the leaf base. The side incisions on each lobe do not cut as deeply toward the midrib as do some other dissectums, and are not as delicate. The whole leaf appears a little coarser than that of most red dissectums. This plant originated with Guldemond of the Netherlands, who sold the stock plants and propagating rights to Le Faber and Company of Boskoop. Later, propagation rights were given to Hauenstein, Rafz CH, of Switzerland. It has become a popular cultivar with nursdwarf -green This name, which means "one's own style or manner," is certainly suitable for this cultivar. The foliage is most distinctive. The leaves appear small and delicate, although measurements show them to be larger than they look. The smaller leaves are 2-4 cm long and wide, while the larger leaves measure 6-8 cm long and 6-9 cm wide. These dimensions are misleading since the leaves are so long and slender that they appear much more delicate than indicated. Each leaf has three lobes, sometimes five, which separate entirely to the leaf base. The lobes almost form a T. They are elongate-lanceolate, narrow at the base, tapering to a narrow tip. While the lobe may measure 5-6 cm long, it does not exceed 1 cm in width. However, it is not as parallel-sided as cultivars in the Linearilobum Group. The margins are complex—deeply toothed to lobulate or combinations of both. The lobes do not lie flat but twist sideways, curl up or down, or become slightly sickle shaped. This variation occurs between leaves or even on the same leaf. The entire appearance of the foliage is rather disorganized, but it is attractive. The colors also vary. Basically the foliage is medium to light green. New foliage has a definite red overtone, which may persist around the margins. Some older foliage also assumes a red tone in full light. This compact dwarf tends to produce indefinite directions of the twigs, much as with the foliage. It is semiprostrate in habit but also has some shoots growing erect. The nodes on the twigs are very close together. Duncan and Davies Nursery of New Zealand raised this amazing dwarf cultivar. In spring the deeply divided leaves are delicate shades of pink to light cream, sparsely flecked with dark and medium green spots and small patches. The creamy areas turn a pale yellow green and the main veins become green as the leaf matures, but the attractive pink tones persist all through the summer. The fiveor seven-lobed leaves are divided almost to the leaf base, and are 7-10 cm long and 7-12 cm wide— surprisingly large for such a dwarf plant. The lobes are narrowly ovate with tail-like pointed tips, 5. 5-9 cm long by 1. 5-2. 5 cm wide at the broadest point in the lower third, and narrowing to 3-8 mm wide at the lobe junctions which are 3-10 mm from the leaf base. The margins have large coarse double teeth. The slender pink petioles are 2. 5-5 cm long.

rhs.description: Vigorous, deciduous shrubby tree about 4m tall with a cascading habit. Leaves with deeply dissected 7 lobes, are rich brownish-red throughout summer, slightly brighter in autumn. Small purplish spring flowers are followed by red fruits in summer

attributes.suggested_uses: Cottage/Informal Garden, City/Courtyard Gardens, Patio/Container Plants
attributes.hort_group_description: Acers in this dissectum group have fine, feathery, deeply divided leaves with finely serrated edges

care.cultivation: Grow in any moisture-retentive, well-drained soil in a sheltered position. Leaf colour is best in full sun which can be tolerated if soil is reliably moist. Leaf scorch can be caused by lack of soil moisture or excessive exposure. Suits container cultivation but attention to watering is needed in dry spells during the growing season. See Japanese maples cultivation
care.pruning: Pruning group 1 , if necessary, from late autumn to midwinter only
care.propagation: Propagate by grafting or softwood cuttings

resistance.pest: May be susceptible to Acer gall mite, aphids , caterpillars and horse chestnut scale
resistance.disease: May be susceptible to Verticillium wilt , acer leaf scorch and honey fungus

care.cultivation: 宜栽植于保水性良好且排水通畅的土壤中，种植位置应避风。叶色在全日照下表现最佳；若土壤湿度稳定，也可耐受充足阳光。土壤缺水或暴露过度时易发生叶灼。亦适合容器栽培，但生长季干旱时需特别注意浇水。另见 Japanese maples cultivation。

rhs_zh.description: 生长旺盛的落叶灌木状小乔木，高约 4 米，具下垂开展的树形。 叶片深裂为 7 裂，整个夏季呈浓褐红色，秋季色泽略更鲜亮。 春季开小型紫色花，夏季随后结红色果实。

attributes.hort_group_description: dissectum 组的槭树具有细致、羽毛状、深裂的叶片，叶缘具细锯齿。

descriptions_zh.preferred: 这个品种最突出的特点是叶色和长势。 叶色为宝石石榴石般浓郁的红橙色。 栽于阴处时，叶片会保留一些绿色调；在阳光充足的位置，则能更好地显现石榴石般的色泽。 其生长势强，最终高度可达 4 米或更高。 若施肥非常充足，幼株可抽生长达 1 米的新梢；但在园林种植环境中，枝条通常不会这么长，株形也更容易整齐成形。 它具有 Dissectum 类型常见的下垂开展习性，随着植株成熟，会形成优美的瀑布状圆丘形树姿。 对裂叶枫而言，其叶片偏大，且深色能良好保持到夏季。 施肥充足的幼株，其叶裂片可长达 12 厘米，不过多数较短。 7 个裂片均完全分裂至叶基。 每个裂片两侧的次级裂刻不像某些其他 Dissectum 类型那样深切向中脉，因此整体不那么纤细，整片叶看起来也比大多数红叶裂叶型更粗犷一些。 该品种源于荷兰的 Guldemond，后者将母株及繁殖权售予 Boskoop 的 Le Faber and Company，之后繁殖权又授予瑞士 Rafz CH 的 Hauenstein。 该品种后来在苗圃业中广受欢迎。 “dwarf -green” 这一名称意为“自己的风格或方式”，确实很适合这个品种。 其叶片极具特色。 叶子看起来小巧而纤细，尽管实际测量显示比视觉感受稍大。 较小的叶片长宽为 2-4 厘米，较大的叶片长 6-8 厘米、宽 6-9 厘米。 不过这些尺寸具有误导性，因为叶片非常细长，看起来远比数字所示更精致。 每片叶具 3 裂，有时 5 裂，均完全分裂至叶基，裂片几乎形成 T 字形。 裂片为狭长披针形，基部狭窄，渐尖成细长尖端。 单个裂片虽可长 5-6 厘米，但宽度不超过 1 厘米。 不过，它并不像 Linearilobum Group 品种那样呈明显平行边。 叶缘形态复杂，深锯齿至浅裂小裂片，或二者兼有。 裂片并不平展，而会向侧面扭转、向上或向下卷曲，或略呈镰刀形。 这种变化可能发生在不同叶片之间，甚至同一片叶上。 整体叶貌较为不规则，但颇具观赏性。 叶色也有变化，基本为中绿至浅绿色。 新叶带有明显红色调，且这种红晕可能持续保留在叶缘；部分老叶在全光照下也会呈现红色调。 这个紧凑的矮生品种，其小枝的生长方向也像叶片一样不定。 株形半匍匐，但也会有部分枝条直立生长。 枝条节间极短。 该惊艳的矮生品种由新西兰 Duncan and Davies Nursery 育出。 春季时，其深裂叶呈柔和的粉色至浅奶油色，并零星点缀深绿和中绿色斑点及小斑块。 随着叶片成熟，奶油色部分转为浅黄绿色，主脉变绿，但迷人的粉色调可持续整个夏季。 叶通常具 5 或 7 裂，几乎分裂至叶基，长 7-10 厘米、宽 7-12 厘米，对于如此矮小的植株而言可谓相当大。 裂片狭卵形，先端具尾状尖，长 5. 5-9 厘米，在下部三分之一处最宽为 1. 5-2. 5 厘米，在裂片连接处收窄至 3-8 毫米宽，而这些连接处距叶基仅 3-10 毫米。 叶缘具粗大的重锯齿。 细长的粉色叶柄长 2. 5-5 厘米。 ‘Geisha’ 是生长缓慢、丛生的矮生品种，最终高约 1 米，冠幅也大致相同。 它是一个鲜明而极为特别的品种，与其他任何矮生品种都不同；从其柔和的综合色来看，它也稍显娇嫩，需要遮护和半阴环境。 它是极佳的庭院植物，也非常适合容器栽培。 ‘Germaine's Gyration’：绿色裂叶型。 这种线裂叶日本枫的生长势强于大多数 Dissectum 类型，因此其下垂的枝条会扭转并起伏波动，这也正是名称中 “gyration” 一词的由来。 其叶片在最宽处再次分裂为次级裂片，但不像大多数 Dissectum 类型那样分裂得那么深。 次级裂片几乎只是较大的齿，仅向中脉方向延伸约一半，并且本身也具粗锯齿。 夏季叶色深绿，秋季转为优美的黄、橙、红综合色。 与多数 Dissectum 类型一样，该品种形成瀑布状、蘑菇形圆丘株形，但横向开展明显大于高度。
